system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: Thermal expansion mismatch and redox-induced volume change stress at the anode-electrolyte interface
USER CONSTRAINT: 200 start-stop cycles at 750°C with >0.35 W/cm² at 0.7V
CALCULATED: Ni-YSZ anode experiences ~25-30% volume expansion during oxidation (based on Ni to NiO transformation density difference)
ASSUMPTION: Current anode has ~40 vol% Ni phase, creating significant dimensional instability during cycling

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Add 5-8 vol% ceria-based redox buffer (e.g., Gd-doped ceria) to the Ni-YSZ anode composite
2. Modify anode fabrication to include a graded transition layer (50-100 μm thick) with increasing ceria content toward the electrolyte interface
3. Implement controlled atmosphere sintering with optimized heating/cooling rates (2-3°C/min) to minimize thermal stress
4. Use commercially available NiO-YSZ and Gd-doped ceria powders (standard SOFC suppliers)
5. Apply screen printing for graded layer deposition, requiring no new equipment
ASSUMPTION: Graded layer can be manufactured with standard SOFC processing techniques

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
Implementation burden is moderate, requiring only material formulation changes and a modified sintering profile. Standard practice uses undoped Ni-YSZ anodes without redox buffers. The added complexity is in the graded layer fabrication, which adds ~15-20% processing time but uses existing equipment. The cost increase is estimated at 10-15% per cell due to additional materials. This is justified by the extended cycle life and reduced stack replacement frequency.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Subject cells to 200 start-stop cycles between room temperature and 750°C with 1-hour dwell at temperature. Hold potential at 0.7V during operation. Monitor cell voltage, stack pressure, and visual inspection for cracks/delamination after every 20 cycles.
Instruments: Electronic load, thermocouples, digital microscope, acoustic emission sensor for crack detection.
Pass threshold: Voltage degradation <10% after 200 cycles, no visual cracks or delamination, power density maintained >0.35 W/cm² at 0.7V.
Duration: Test period ~3 months (allowing 1 day per cycle including conditioning time).
ASSUMPTION: Test can be accelerated with 2-hour cycles while maintaining the same thermal profile without affecting failure mechanisms.
